claims.statement: Bitru is a figure of demonology also known as Sidragaso, Sytry or Sitri.
claims.statement_id: Bitru adalah tokoh demonologi yang juga dikenal sebagai Sidragaso, Sytry, atau Sitri.
claims.quote: Bitru es un personaje perteneciente a la demonología. También es conocido como Sidragaso, Sytry o Sitri

claims.statement: A great prince of hell, he has the form of a leopard with griffin's wings but can also appear as a very handsome human, and commands 70 legions.
claims.statement_id: Ia pangeran agung neraka berwujud macan tutul bersayap griffin, yang juga dapat muncul sebagai manusia sangat tampan, dan memimpin 70 legiun.
claims.quote: Gran príncipe de los infiernos, tiene la forma de un leopardo con alas de grifo, pero también puede aparecer bajo una forma humana muy hermosa. Comanda 70 legiones

claims.statement: His task is to inflame men with lust for women and vice versa; when he pleases he reveals women's secrets, always making them look ridiculous.
claims.statement_id: Tugasnya mengobarkan nafsu lelaki terhadap perempuan dan sebaliknya; bila ia mau, ia membuka rahasia perempuan dan selalu mempermalukan mereka.
claims.quote: es el encargado de inflamar de lujuria al hombre hacia la mujer y viceversa. Descubre, cuando le parece, los secretos de las mujeres, a quienes siempre pone en ridículo.

claims.statement: "Sytry ou Bitru" is a great prince in hell who appears in the form of a leopard with griffin's wings.
claims.statement_id: "Sytry ou Bitru" adalah pangeran agung di neraka yang tampil berupa macan tutul bersayap griffon.
claims.quote: Sytry ou Bitru, grand prince aux enfers ; il apparaît sous la forme d’un léopard, avec des ailes de griffon.

claims.statement: When he takes human form he is of great beauty; it is he who inflames the passions.
claims.statement_id: Ketika ia mengambil rupa manusia, ia sangat rupawan; dialah yang mengobarkan nafsu.
claims.quote: Mais lorsqu’il prend la forme humaine, il est d’une grande beauté. C’est lui qui enflamme les passions.

claims.statement: He reveals women's secrets when commanded, which he gladly turns to ridicule; seventy legions obey him.
claims.statement_id: Ia membuka rahasia para perempuan bila diperintah, dan senang menjadikannya bahan olok-olok; tujuh puluh legiun menaatinya.
claims.quote: Il découvre, quand on le lui commande, les secrets des femmes, qu’il tourne volontiers en ridicule. Soixante-dix légions lui obéissent.

claims.statement: He also likes to excite women into showing themselves naked and inspires them to despise modesty.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga suka membangkitkan hasrat perempuan agar menampakkan diri tanpa busana dan mengilhami mereka untuk meremehkan rasa malu.
claims.quote: También le gusta excitarlas para que se muestren desnudas y les inspira a despreciar el pudor.

claims.statement: The bocarrot is a kind of genie of Catalan mythology related to the Greek satyrs and Roman fauns; in old popular belief it lived in wheat fields and spurred the plants' growth.
claims.statement_id: Bocarrot adalah semacam roh mitologi Katalan yang berkerabat dengan satir Yunani dan faun Romawi; menurut kepercayaan lama ia tinggal di ladang gandum dan merangsang pertumbuhan tanamannya.
claims.quote: El bocarrot és una mena de geni propi de la mitologia catalana. Emparentat amb els sàtirs grecs i els faunes romans, segons les antigues creences populars vivia als camps de blat i n'estimulava el creixement de les plantes

claims.statement: If a reaper suddenly fell ill it was because he had stumbled on the bocarrot, which hid among the ears of wheat until caught with the last stroke of the sickle.
claims.statement_id: Bila seorang penuai tiba-tiba sakit, itu karena ia tersandung bocarrot, yang bersembunyi di antara bulir gandum sampai tertangkap pada ayunan sabit terakhir.
claims.quote: Si un segador es trobava malalt de forma sobtada era perquè havia ensopegat amb el bocarrot, que s'anava amagant entre les espigues fins que era capturat amb l'últim cop de falç.

claims.statement: The bocarrot is invisible and can grow larger or smaller at will.
claims.statement_id: Bocarrot tidak terlihat dan dapat membesar atau mengecil sesuka hati.
claims.quote: El bocarrot és invisible i es pot fer més gran o més petit a voluntat.

claims.statement: In Samalús, Vallès Oriental, the last wheat was called the bocarrot, and the last clump left to reap was called the boc (billy goat) or cabra (nanny goat).
claims.statement_id: Di Samalús, Vallès Oriental, gandum terakhir disebut bocarrot, dan rumpun terakhir yang belum dituai disebut boc (kambing jantan) atau cabra (kambing betina).
claims.quote: A Samalús, Vallès Oriental, es coneixia com a "bocarrot" el darrer blat, mentre que de la darrera mota de blat que quedava per segar se'n deia "boc" o "cabra".

claims.statement: In Gósol, Berguedà, reapers believed in a wheat spirit called el boc, the spirit of the last wheat; whoever caught the bocarrot secured the field's yield, wealth and prosperity.
claims.statement_id: Di Gósol, Berguedà, para penuai percaya pada roh gandum bernama el boc, roh gandum terakhir; siapa yang menangkap bocarrot menjamin hasil ladang, kekayaan, dan kemakmuran.
claims.quote: A Gósol, Berguedà, els antics segadors creien en un geni del blat que anomenaven "el boc", l'esperit del darrer blat. Qui agafava el "bocarrot" s'assegurava el rendiment del camp, riquesa i prosperitat.

claims.statement: A modern illustrated calendar of Catalan mythology describes the bocarrot as descended from the genies of the Stone Age.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kalender bergambar modern tentang mitologi Katalan menggambarkan bocarrot sebagai keturunan para genius Zaman Batu.
claims.quote: Descendent dels genis de l'Edat de Pedra

claims.statement: Among reaping crews it was said that a bocarrot lived in every wheat field and stimulated the plants so that they gave good-sized, abundant grain.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan rombongan penuai dikatakan bahwa tiap ladang gandum dihuni seekor bocarrot yang merangsang tanaman sehingga bijinya berukuran baik dan melimpah.
claims.quote: Entre les colles de segadors es deia que a cada bladar hi vivia un bocarrot, que estimulava la ... de les plantes i que donessin gra de bona mida i abundant.

claims.statement: In demonology Glasya-Labolas (also spelled Caacrinolaas, Caassimolar or Classyalabolas) is a mighty President of hell commanding thirty-six legions of demons.
claims.statement_id: Dalam demonologi, Glasya-Labolas (juga ditulis Caacrinolaas, Caassimolar, atau Classyalabolas) adalah Presiden neraka yang berkuasa dan memimpin tiga puluh enam legiun iblis.
claims.quote: Na demonologia, Glasya-Labolas (também grafado Caacrinolaas, Caassimolar, Classyalabolas, Glassia-labolis ou Glasya Labolas) é poderoso Presidente (e Fidalgo para outros autores) do Inferno e comanda trinta e seis legiões de demônios.

claims.statement: He is described as the Great President of hell, able to grant talent in the fine arts and inspire a great thirst for blood in men.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai Presiden Agung neraka yang dapat memberi bakat seni rupa dan membangkitkan haus darah pada manusia.
claims.quote: é descrito como o Grande Presidente do Inferno, que pode conceder talento nas Belas Artes e inspirar nos homens uma grande sede de sangue.

claims.statement: He is the captain and author of murders and bloodshed, and tells of things past and to come.
claims.statement_id: Ia pemimpin dan biang pembunuhan serta pertumpahan darah, dan memberi tahu hal-hal masa lalu dan masa depan.
claims.quote: Ele é o capitão e autor, no que diz respeito aos homicídios e derramamento de sangue, diz a todos, as coisas sobre o passado e no que há de acontecer

claims.statement: He can cause love between friends and foes, incite murder, and make a man invisible.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat menimbulkan cinta antara kawan dan lawan, menghasut pembunuhan, dan membuat orang tidak terlihat.
claims.quote: causando-lhes o amor entre eles, e se o desejar, incita a cometer homicídios e pode fazer de um homem invisível.

claims.statement: He is depicted as a dog with the wings of a griffin.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai anjing bersayap griffin.
claims.quote: Ele é retratado como um cão com as asas de um Grifo.

claims.statement: "Caacrinolaas", also called Caassimolar and Glassialabolas, is a great president in hell who appears as a dog, with a dog's gait, with griffin's wings.
claims.statement_id: "Caacrinolaas", juga disebut Caassimolar dan Glassialabolas, adalah presiden agung di neraka yang tampil sebagai anjing, berjalan seperti anjing, dengan sayap griffon.
claims.quote: Caacrinolaas, nommé aussi Caassimolar et Glassialabolas, grand président aux enfers, il se présente sous la forme d’un chien, et il en a la démarche, avec des ailes de griffon.

claims.statement: He gives knowledge of the liberal arts and, by a strange contrast, inspires homicides; it is said that he predicts the future well.
claims.statement_id: Ia memberi pengetahuan tentang seni-seni liberal dan, secara kontras aneh, mengilhami pembunuhan; dikatakan ia meramalkan masa depan dengan baik.
claims.quote: Il donne la connaissance des arts libéraux, et, par un bizarre contraste, il inspire les homicides. On y dit qu’il prédit bien l’avenir.

claims.statement: This demon makes a man invisible and commands thirty-six legions.
claims.statement_id: Iblis ini membuat manusia tak terlihat dan memimpin tiga puluh enam legiun.
claims.quote: Ce démon rend l’homme invisible et commande trente-six légions.

claims.statement: The Grand Grimoire calls him Classyalabolas and makes him only a kind of sergeant who sometimes serves as a mount for Nébiros or Naberus.
claims.statement_id: Le Grand Grimoire menyebutnya Classyalabolas dan hanya menjadikannya semacam sersan yang kadang menjadi tunggangan Nébiros atau Naberus.
claims.quote: Le Grand Grimoire le nomme Classyalabolas, et n’en fait qu’une espèce de sergent qui sert quelquefois de monture à Nébiros ou Naberus.

claims.statement: The cabicanca is a legendary bird-shaped creature of Portuguese popular tradition and superstition.
claims.statement_id: Cabicanca adalah makhluk legendaris berwujud burung dalam tradisi dan takhayul rakyat Portugal.
claims.quote: A cabicanca é uma criatura lendária com forma de pássaro das tradições e superstições populares portuguesas.

claims.statement: One day a bird never before seen in Aguiar landed on the church tower, and the locals stopped going to Mass.
claims.statement_id: Suatu hari seekor burung yang belum pernah terlihat di Aguiar hinggap di menara gereja, dan penduduk berhenti pergi ke misa.
claims.quote: Pousou um dia na torre da Igreja um pássaro, jamais visto por terras de Aguiar. As gentes do lugar deixaram de ir à missa

claims.statement: People exclaimed "Que bicanca!" ("What a beak!"), the source of the name cabicanca.
claims.statement_id: Orang-orang berseru "Que bicanca!" ("Paruh yang luar biasa!"), asal nama cabicanca.
claims.quote: Que bicanca, Santo Deus, que bicanca!

claims.statement: A muleteer named Martinho Afonso shot it; one accurate shot brought down the stork, and Afonso was carried shoulder-high.
claims.statement_id: Seorang pengangkut barang bernama Martinho Afonso menembaknya; satu tembakan tepat menjatuhkan bangau itu, dan Afonso diarak di atas bahu.
claims.quote: Bastou um tiro certeiro, que ecoou por toda a região, para que a cegonha sucumbisse e Afonso fosse erguido em ombros.

claims.statement: The story endures, and the name cabicanca has stuck to the people of Aguiar, who fondly adopted it as their own.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini bertahan dan nama cabicanca melekat pada warga Aguiar, yang mengadopsinya dengan sayang.
claims.quote: A história perdura e o nome "cabicanca" ficou para sempre ligado aos aguiarenses que, carinhosamente, o adoptaram como seu.

claims.statement: A tower is also known as the Torre da Cabicanca because of its connection with the legend of a cursed stork that terrorised the inhabitants.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah menara juga dikenal sebagai Torre da Cabicanca karena kaitannya dengan legenda seekor bangau terkutuk yang meneror penduduk.
claims.quote: É também conhecida por Torre da Cabicanca, por se relacionar com a lenda de uma cegonha amaldiçoada que aterrorizava os habitantes.

claims.statement: In the 17th century gargoyles were installed on the tower, which was then also designated the Torre da Cabicanca, relating it to the legend of a stork that terrorized the inhabitants.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-17 sejumlah gargoyle dipasang pada menara itu, yang saat itu juga disebut Torre da Cabicanca, mengaitkannya dengan legenda seekor bangau yang meneror penduduk.
claims.quote: In the 17th century, gargoyles were installed on the tower, also designated at the time as the Torre da Cabicanca, which related it to the legend of a stork that terrorized the inhabitants.

claims.statement: A cabraboc is a fantastic being of Catalan folk imagination, half human above and half goat below.
claims.statement_id: Cabraboc adalah makhluk khayalan imajinasi rakyat Katalan, setengah manusia di bagian atas dan setengah kambing di bagian bawah.
claims.quote: Un cabraboc és un ésser fantàstic propi de l'imaginari popular català, mig humà per la part de dalt i mig cabra o boc per la part de baix.

claims.statement: Cabrabocs are said to chase men as if they were nanny goats and women as if they were billy goats; they are forest beings to be avoided when travelling at night.
claims.statement_id: Para cabraboc konon mengejar lelaki seperti kambing betina dan perempuan seperti kambing jantan; mereka makhluk hutan yang harus dihindari saat bepergian malam.
claims.quote: Es diu que els cabrabocs persegueixen els homes com si fossin cabres i les dones com si fossin bocs. Són éssers del bosc i cal evitar-los quan es viatja de nit

claims.statement: The chases often end with the victim falling off a cliff, and they were sometimes described with bat wings.
claims.statement_id: Pengejaran itu sering berakhir dengan korban terjatuh dari tebing, dan kadang mereka digambarkan bersayap kelelawar.
claims.quote: sovint, les persecucions acaben fent estimbar la víctima per un penya-segat. Algunes vegades, se'ls descrivia amb ales de ratapinyada.

claims.statement: In the Ripollet legend El vell i la vella, a cat came out of an old couple's basket and turned into one more devil, the Cabraboc.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda Ripollet El vell i la vella, seekor kucing keluar dari keranjang sepasang orang tua dan berubah menjadi iblis, si Cabraboc.
claims.quote: Aleshores, del cistell en sortí un gat que es convertí en un diable més, el Cabraboc.

claims.statement: The Diables de Caldes de Montbui give the name cabraboc to the helmet worn by their main devil, Llucifer.
claims.statement_id: Kelompok Diables de Caldes de Montbui menamai cabraboc helm yang dipakai iblis utama mereka, Llucifer.
claims.quote: Els Diables de Caldes de Montbui donen el nom de cabraboc al casc que porta el diable principal, que anomenen Llucifer.

claims.statement: Les Bruixes de Ripollet stage the legend at the children's carnival, and the Diables de Ripollet carry it at the head of Saturday's carnival parade.
claims.statement_id: Les Bruixes de Ripollet mementaskan legenda ini pada karnaval anak, dan Diables de Ripollet membawanya di depan pawai karnaval hari Sabtu.
claims.quote: Les Bruixes de Ripollet n'escenifiquen la llegenda durant el carnaval infantil, i els Diables de Ripollet el treuen al capdavant de la rua de Carnaval de dissabte.

claims.statement: The Cabraboc is a being half person on the upper part and half goat and billy goat on the lower part.
claims.statement_id: Cabraboc adalah makhluk setengah manusia di bagian atas dan setengah kambing betina dan kambing jantan di bagian bawah.
claims.quote: El Cabraboc és un ésser mig persona per la part de dalt i mig cabra i boc per la part de sota.

claims.statement: The legend says that in Ripollet on Carnival day an old man and an old woman went out for a walk; the old woman carried a basket with a pot inside, and everything suggested it held their lunch.
claims.statement_id: Legenda mengatakan bahwa di Ripollet pada hari Karnaval seorang kakek dan nenek keluar berjalan-jalan; sang nenek membawa keranjang berisi panci, dan segalanya menunjukkan bahwa itu bekal makan siang.
claims.quote: Explica la llegenda que a Ripollet la diada de Carnestoltes van sortir a passejar un vell i una vella. La vella portava un cistell amb una olla dins, tot feia pensar que hi portava el dinar.

claims.statement: One of the little devils saw the old woman and her basket and struck the pot with a stick; instead of stew a cat came out of it, which by magic in no time turned into a cabraboc.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu iblis kecil melihat si nenek dan keranjangnya lalu memukul panci dengan tongkat; alih-alih sup, keluar seekor kucing yang secara ajaib seketika berubah menjadi cabraboc.
claims.quote: Un dels diablots va veure la vella i el cistell i va pensar: “Ara és la meva”, i amb un bastó que portava va donar un cop a l’olla. Tothom es va quedar parat, perquè de l’olla, en lloc d’escudella, en va sortir un gat, que per art de màgia i en un tres i no res es va convertir en cabraboc.

claims.statement: The event was talked about so much that from then on, every year at Carnival, the comparsa groups portray it.
claims.statement_id: Peristiwa itu begitu banyak dibicarakan sehingga sejak itu setiap tahun saat Karnaval kelompok-kelompok comparsa menampilkannya.
claims.quote: Se’n va parlar tant, del fet, que des de llavors cada any per Carnaval les colles de comparses el representen.

claims.statement: The Cagrino, also known as Guecubu, is an evil spirit in the folklore of the continental Roma.
claims.statement_id: Cagrino, dikenal juga sebagai Guecubu, adalah roh jahat dalam cerita rakyat orang Rom di daratan Eropa.
claims.quote: Il Cagrino, conosciuto anche come Guecubu, è uno spirito maligno secondo il folklore dei rom continentali.

claims.statement: The myth originates in north-western India, where the spirit is called Harginn.
claims.statement_id: Mitos ini berasal dari wilayah barat laut India, tempat roh itu disebut Harginn.
claims.quote: Il mito ha origine dalle regioni nord-occidentali dell'India, dove lo spirito viene chiamato Harginn .

claims.statement: It has the form of a yellow hedgehog about 50 cm long and 20 wide, and rides horses to exhaustion at night.
claims.statement_id: Ia berwujud landak kuning sepanjang sekitar 50 cm dan lebar 20 cm, dan menunggangi kuda pada malam hari sampai kuda itu kelelahan.
claims.quote: Ha la forma di un riccio giallo, lungo circa 50 cm, largo 20. Cavalca i cavalli fino allo sfinimento nella notte

claims.statement: The next day the horses look sick and exhausted, with tangled manes and drenched in sweat.
claims.statement_id: Esok harinya kuda-kuda itu tampak sakit dan lelah, surainya kusut, dan basah kuyup oleh keringat.
claims.quote: il giorno dopo appaiono malati ed esausti, con la criniera arruffata e in un bagno di sudore.

claims.statement: As a remedy, the horses are tied to a stake rubbed with garlic, with a red thread forming a cross at its foot.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menangkalnya, kuda diikat pada tiang yang telah digosok bawang putih, dengan benang merah berbentuk salib di kakinya.
claims.quote: i cavalli vengono legati a un bastone su cui è stato precedentemente strofinato dell'aglio, ai piedi del quale viene posto un filo rosso formante una croce

claims.statement: It has the form of a hedgehog, is yellow in colour, and is a foot and a half in length and a span in breadth.
claims.statement_id: Ia berbentuk landak, berwarna kuning, panjangnya satu setengah kaki dan lebarnya sejengkal.
claims.quote: It has the form of a hedgehog, is yellow- in colour, and is a foot and a half in length and a span in breadth.

claims.statement: Horses are the special prey of the Chagrin, who rides them into a state of exhaustion, as does the Guecubu of Chili; the next day they appear sick and weary, with tangled manes and bathed in sweat.
claims.statement_id: Kuda adalah mangsa khusus Chagrin, yang menungganginya sampai kelelahan, seperti halnya Guecubu dari Chili; keesokan harinya kuda tampak sakit dan lesu, dengan surai kusut dan bersimbah keringat.
claims.quote: Horses are the special prey of the Chagrin, who rides them into a state of exhaustion, as does the Guecubu (q.v.) of Chili. The next day they appear sick and weary, with tangled manes and bathed in sweat.

claims.statement: When this is observed the horses are tethered to a stake rubbed with garlic juice and a red thread is laid on the ground in the form of a cross, or some of the animal's hair is mixed with salt, meal and bat's blood, cooked to bread and smeared on the hoof.
claims.statement_id: Bila hal ini terlihat, kuda diikat pada tiang yang digosok sari bawang putih dan benang merah dibentangkan di tanah membentuk salib, atau sebagian bulu hewan itu dicampur garam, tepung, dan darah kelelawar, dimasak menjadi roti lalu dioleskan pada kukunya.
claims.quote: When this is observed they are tethered to a stake which has been rubbed with garlic juice, then a red thread is laid on the ground in the form of a cross, or else some of the hair of the animal is mixed with salt, meal and the blood of a bat and cooked to bread, with which the hoof of the horse is smeared.

claims.statement: The calygreyhound is a mythical creature of medieval heraldry; the de Vere family, Earls of Oxford, used it in their arms in the 15th and 16th centuries.
claims.statement_id: Calygreyhound adalah makhluk mitos dalam heraldik abad pertengahan; keluarga de Vere, Earl of Oxford, memakainya pada lambang mereka pada abad ke-15 dan ke-16.
claims.quote: The calygreyhound is a mythical creature that appears on medieval heraldry. The de Vere family, who were the Earls of Oxford, used the calygreyhound in their coat of arms in the 15th and 16th centuries.

claims.statement: The calygreyhound may be unique to the de Veres, and unlike most heraldic monsters it made no attempt to look realistic.
claims.statement_id: Calygreyhound mungkin khas keluarga de Vere, dan tidak seperti kebanyakan monster heraldik, ia tidak berusaha tampak realistis.
claims.quote: The calygreyhound may be unique to the de Veres, and unlike most heraldic monsters, it made no attempt to seem realistic.

claims.statement: It is consistently described with a wildcat's head, a deer's or antelope's body, eagle's claws on the forefeet, ox hooves, antlers or horns, a lion's or ox's hind legs, and a tail like a lion's or poodle's.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan berkepala kucing liar, bertubuh rusa atau antelop, bercakar elang di kaki depan, berkuku lembu, bertanduk, berkaki belakang singa atau lembu, dan berekor seperti singa atau pudel.
claims.quote: The calygreyhound is described consistently as having the head of a wildcat, the torso of a deer or antelope, the claws of an eagle on its forefeet, ox hooves, antlers or horns, the hind legs of a lion or ox, and its tail like a lion or poodle.

claims.statement: Occasionally it is shown with eagle's wings, and it is said to represent speed or swiftness.
claims.statement_id: Sesekali ia digambarkan bersayap elang, dan konon melambangkan kecepatan.
claims.quote: On some rare occasions, the Calygreyhound may be seen as depicted with the wings of an eagle. It is said to represent speed or swiftness.

claims.statement: The calygreyhound is generally thought to be the artist's invention, though some of its parts are based on reality.
claims.statement_id: Umumnya calygreyhound dianggap rekaan seniman saja, meski sebagian unsurnya berdasarkan kenyataan.
claims.quote: It is generally accepted that the calygreyhound is simply a figment of the artist's imagination, but some parts of it are based on reality.

claims.statement: An article on Tudor heraldic monsters presents the calygreyhound as one of the Tudor oddities and a favourite with the de Vere family, Earls of Oxford.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah artikel tentang monster heraldik zaman Tudor menampilkan calygreyhound sebagai salah satu keanehan Tudor dan favorit keluarga de Vere, para Earl of Oxford.
claims.quote: Finally, here is perhaps the most extraordinary of all these Tudor oddities, a favourite with the de Vere family, Earls of Oxford

claims.statement: The calygreyhound is shown in a drawing by Colin Cole made from the de Vere family's contemporary seal.
claims.statement_id: Calygreyhound ditampilkan dalam gambar karya Colin Cole yang dibuat dari segel sezaman milik keluarga de Vere.
claims.quote: Calygreyhound, drawn here by Colin Cole from their contemporary seal (from Dennys 1975).

claims.statement: Camunyes is a child-scaring bogey of Catalan folk imagination, an evil being with a big mouth and long fangs that eats the children it carries off when it comes down from the roofs and attics where it lives.
claims.statement_id: Camunyes adalah momok penakut anak imajinasi rakyat Katalan, makhluk jahat bermulut besar dan bertaring panjang yang memakan anak-anak yang diculiknya saat turun dari atap dan loteng tempat tinggalnya.
claims.quote: En Camunyes és un espantamainades propi de l'imaginari popular català. Es tracta d'un ésser malèfic que té una boca grossa i llargs ullals amb què es menja els nens que s'enduu quan baixa dels terrats i les golfes, on viu.

claims.statement: The figure is especially known in the Terra Alta; legend says he was a flesh-and-blood man who became a monster after seeing his brother killed.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh ini terkenal di Terra Alta; menurut legenda ia dahulu manusia biasa yang berubah menjadi monster setelah melihat saudaranya dibunuh.
claims.quote: Personatge especialment conegut a la Terra Alta, segons la llegenda era un home de carn i ossos que es va convertir en un ésser monstruós en veure com mataven el seu germà.

claims.statement: En Camunyes is a big beast with a large mouth and long fangs that used to swallow children.
claims.statement_id: En Camunyes adalah binatang buas bermulut besar dan bertaring panjang yang dulu menelan anak-anak.
claims.quote: En Camunyes és una bestiota de boca gran i llargs ullals que engolia els nens.

claims.statement: It is said to live on the roofs and in the attics, from which it comes down to carry off children.
claims.statement_id: Konon ia tinggal di atap dan loteng, dan dari sana turun untuk membawa pergi anak-anak.
claims.quote: Es diu que viu als terrats i a les golfes, de les quals baixa per emportar-se els nens.

claims.statement: A list of child-scaring figures records Camunyes in the Terra Alta as a small animal-like ogre with big teeth that swallows naughty children as if they were "marenga".
claims.statement_id: Sebuah daftar tokoh penakut-nakut anak mencatat Camunyes di Terra Alta sebagai raksasa pemakan manusia seperti binatang, kecil dan bergigi besar, yang menelan anak nakal seolah-olah mereka "marenga".
claims.quote: CAMUNYES Terra Alta Ogre animal, menut i amb grans dents. Engoleix els nens dolents com si fossin marenga

claims.statement: Among Catalan child-scaring figures, some have world counterparts such as the Papu, the Home del sac and witches, while others are quite their own and genuine, such as lo Marraco, en Camunyes and en Rosegacebes.
claims.statement_id: Di antara tokoh penakut-nakut anak Katalan, sebagian punya padanan dunia seperti Papu, Home del sac, dan para penyihir, sedangkan yang lain sepenuhnya khas dan asli, seperti lo Marraco, en Camunyes, dan en Rosegacebes.
claims.quote: Hi ha figures mundials que tenen el seu referent a Catalunya com ara el Papu, l'Home del sac i les bruixes i d'altres de ben propis i genuïns com ara lo Marraco, en Camunyes o en Rosegacebes.

claims.statement: The Caquesseitão is a mythological creature in Fernão Mendes Pinto's Peregrinação, which the author insists is a real animal living on the island of Sumatra.
claims.statement_id: Caquesseitão adalah makhluk mitologis dalam Peregrinação karya Fernão Mendes Pinto, yang menurut penulisnya hewan nyata yang hidup di pulau Sumatra.
claims.quote: O Caquesseitão é uma criatura mitológica na obra Peregrinação de Fernão Mendes Pinto (embora o autor garanta ser um animal real) que existiria na ilha de Samatra

claims.statement: Pinto describes it as the size of a large duck, very black, scaled on the back, with a row of quill-length spines along the spine, and bat-like wings.
claims.statement_id: Pinto menggambarkannya sebesar bebek besar, sangat hitam, bersisik di punggung, dengan deretan duri sepanjang pena di sepanjang tulang punggung, dan bersayap seperti kelelawar.
claims.quote: do tamanho de uma grande pata, muito pretos, conchados pelas costas, com uma ordem de espinhos pelo fio do lombo do comprimento de uma pena de escrever e com asas da feição das do morcego

claims.statement: It has a snake's neck, a cockspur-like claw on its forehead, and a very long green-and-black tail like the lizards of that land.
claims.statement_id: Ia berleher ular, bertaji seperti ayam jantan di dahinya, dan berekor sangat panjang bercorak hijau dan hitam seperti kadal di negeri itu.
claims.quote: com pescoço de cobra e uma unha, a modo de esporão de galo na testa, com rabo muito comprido pintado de verde e preto, como são os lagartos desta terra.

claims.statement: These creatures fly in leaps and hunt monkeys and other animals in the treetops for food.
claims.statement_id: Hewan ini terbang dengan cara melompat dan memburu monyet serta hewan lain di atas pohon sebagai makanannya.
claims.quote: Estes bichos de voo, a modo de salto, caçam os bugios e bichos por cima das árvores, dos quais se mantêm.

claims.statement: The Caquesseitão became a frequent presence in Indo-Portuguese art.
claims.statement_id: Caquesseitão sering muncul dalam seni Indo-Portugis.
claims.quote: Tornou-se presença frequente na arte indo-portuguesa.

claims.statement: An animal of fantastic nature, the Caquesseitão was described by Fernão Mendes Pinto in the book "Peregrinação" [1614]; with characteristics of different species, the mysterious creature entered the exotic imagination of the time.
claims.statement_id: Hewan berwatak fantastis, Caquesseitão dilukiskan oleh Fernão Mendes Pinto dalam buku "Peregrinação" [1614]; dengan ciri-ciri berbagai spesies, makhluk misterius ini memasuki imajinasi eksotis zamannya.
claims.quote: An animal of fantastic nature, the Caquesseitão was described by Fernão Mendes Pinto in the book "Peregrinação" [1614]. With characteristics of different species, the mysterious creature entered the exotic imagination of the time.

claims.statement: A Caquesseitão aquamanile dating back to the 17th century would have been manufactured in South China or Southeast Asia; it is excellently executed in repoussé, engraved and chiseled silver.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah aquamanile Caquesseitão dari abad ke-17 diperkirakan dibuat di Tiongkok Selatan atau Asia Tenggara; ia dikerjakan dengan sangat baik dalam perak repoussé, ukiran, dan pahatan.
claims.quote: Dating back to the 17th century, Caquesseitão aquamanil would have been manufactured in South China or Southeast Asia. The piece is excellently executed, using repoussé, engraved and chiseled silver working techniques.

claims.statement: In the old-spelling text of the Peregrinação the narrator says that here they also saw a very new manner and strange shape of beasts that the natives of the land call Caquesseitão, the size of a large duck and very black, with humped backs.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks berejaan lama Peregrinação sang pencerita mengatakan bahwa di sana mereka juga melihat jenis binatang yang sangat baru dan berbentuk aneh, yang oleh penduduk setempat disebut Caquesseitão, sebesar bebek besar dan sangat hitam, berpunggung bongkok.
claims.quote: Vimos aquy tambem hũa muyto noua maneyra, & eﬅranha feyção de bichos, aque os naturaes da terra chamão Caqueſſeitão, do tamanho de hũa grande pata, muyto pretos, conchados pelas coﬅas

claims.statement: The Caragot is a child-scaring bogey of Catalan folk imagination, a huge, almost giant man, a kind of sack man who comes down the chimney and carries off naughty children in a big sack to eat them in soup.
claims.statement_id: Caragot adalah momok penakut anak imajinasi rakyat Katalan, lelaki besar hampir raksasa semacam orang karung yang masuk lewat cerobong asap dan membawa anak nakal dalam karung besar untuk dimakan bersama sup.
claims.quote: El Caragot és un espantamainades propi de l'imaginari popular català. Se'l descriu com un homenot alt, quasi un gegant, una mena d'home del sac que entra a les cases per la xemeneia i se n'enduu els nens entremaliats en un gran sac per a menjar-se'ls amb sopes.

claims.statement: El Caragot is a tall, giant-like man who comes down the chimney with an enormous sack on his back full of mischievous children, with whom he makes soups on the hearth fire; he is similar to the Home del Sac.
claims.statement_id: El Caragot adalah lelaki tinggi dan besar seperti raksasa yang turun lewat cerobong asap membawa karung besar di punggungnya penuh anak-anak nakal, yang ia jadikan sup di atas api perapian; ia mirip dengan Home del Sac.
claims.quote: El Caragot és un homenot alt i agegantat que baixa per la xemeneia amb un enorme sac a l’esquena ple de nens entremaliats, amb els quals es fa unes sopes al foc de la llar. Similar a l’Home del Sac.

claims.statement: A list of child-scaring figures records Caragot, also written Caragol, noted as "com. de Tarragona", as coming down chimneys and making soups of bad children, related to the home del sac.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah daftar tokoh penakut-nakut anak mencatat Caragot, juga ditulis Caragol, dengan keterangan "com. de Tarragona", yang turun lewat cerobong dan menjadikan anak nakal sebagai sup, berkerabat dengan home del sac.
claims.quote: CARAGOT/ CARAGOL com. de Tarragona ... que baixa per les xemeneies i dels nens dolents en fa sopes. Emparentat amb l'home del sac.

claims.statement: A magazine article on the espantanens of the Nit d'Ànimes describes the Caragot as a tall giant-like man who comes down the chimney with an enormous sack full of mischievous children, with whom he makes soups at the hearth fire; similar to the Home del Sac.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah artikel majalah tentang espantanens pada Nit d'Ànimes menggambarkan Caragot sebagai lelaki tinggi seperti raksasa yang turun lewat cerobong dengan karung besar penuh anak nakal, yang ia jadikan sup di perapian; mirip dengan Home del Sac.
claims.quote: El Caragot és un homenot alt i agegantat que baixa per la xemeneia amb un enorme sac a l'esquena ple d'infants entremaliats, amb els quals es fa unes sopes al foc de la llar. Similar a l'Home del Sac.

claims.statement: Catalan Wikipedia lists El Caragot among the espantamainades of Catalonia.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia berbahasa Katalan mencantumkan El Caragot di antara espantamainades di Katalunya.
claims.quote: A Catalunya: L'Ànima de Cantiret En Banya Verda Els Batonis En Camunyes El Caragot La Cardapeçols La Fou

claims.statement: The Cardapeçols is a child-scaring bogey of Catalan folk imagination from around Montserrat.
claims.statement_id: Cardapeçols adalah momok penakut anak imajinasi rakyat Katalan dari sekitar Montserrat.
claims.quote: La Cardapeçols és una espantamainades pròpia de l'imaginari popular català, concretament de la rodalia de Montserrat.

claims.statement: She is a scowling ogress who punishes girls who will not let their hair be combed, like the Moixina, tugging so hard she tears their hair out.
claims.statement_id: Ia raksasa perempuan berwajah garang yang menghukum anak perempuan yang tidak mau disisir, seperti Moixina, dengan menyentak rambut mereka begitu keras hingga tercabut.
claims.quote: Es tracta d'una ogressa malcarada que castiga les nenes que no es deixen pentinar (tal com fa també la Moixina, una altra espantamainades semblant) i els fa unes estrebades tan fortes que els arrenca els cabells

claims.statement: Her name comes from the wool cards she uses to comb her victims.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berasal dari sisir wol (card) yang dipakainya untuk menyisir korbannya.
claims.quote: El nom li ve del fet que per a pentinar les seves víctimes se serveix de cards i aurons per cardar llana d'ovella

claims.statement: According to Joan Amades in the Revista de Dialectología y Tradiciones Populares in 1957, the Cardapeçols is known in El Bruc, Esparraguera and Piera.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan Joan Amades dalam Revista de Dialectología y Tradiciones Populares tahun 1957, Cardapeçols dikenal di El Bruc, Esparraguera, dan Piera.
claims.quote: Segons va recollir Joan Amades en un article a la Revista de Dialectología y Tradiciones Populares el 1957, la Cardapeçols és coneguda al Bruc, Esparraguera i Piera.

claims.statement: She is a strange little woman who combs mischievous girls who do not want to be combed, using wool-carding thorns as a comb.
claims.statement_id: Ia perempuan kecil yang aneh yang menyisir anak perempuan nakal yang tidak mau disisir, memakai duri pengurai wol sebagai sisir.
claims.quote: Doneta estranya que pentina les nenes entremaliades que no volen pentinar-se. Fa servir com a pinta espines de cardar llana.

claims.statement: Catalan Wikipedia lists La Cardapeçols among the espantamainades of Catalonia.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia berbahasa Katalan mencantumkan La Cardapeçols di antara espantamainades di Katalunya.
claims.quote: A Catalunya: L'Ànima de Cantiret En Banya Verda Els Batonis En Camunyes El Caragot La Cardapeçols La Fou

claims.statement: The carro da condeceira is the witches' cart, carrying the devil and the witches dancing inside, and creaking loudly as it passes through villages.
claims.statement_id: Carro da condeceira adalah kereta para penyihir yang membawa iblis dan penyihir yang menari di dalamnya, dan berderit keras saat melewati desa.
claims.quote: O carro da condeceira é o carro das bruxas. O carro conduz o diabo e as bruxas que vão dentro a dançar. O carro faz uma grande chiadeira ao passar pelas aldeias.

claims.statement: The cart travels only at night; once, as it passed along the Rua dos Gatos in Guimarães, a curious man came to the window to look.
claims.statement_id: Kereta itu hanya berjalan malam hari; suatu kali saat melewati Rua dos Gatos di Guimarães, seorang yang penasaran melongok dari jendela.
claims.quote: O carro da condeceira é o carro das Bruxas, que anda só de noite. Uma vez ia ele a passar pela Rua-dos-gatos (Guimarães), e um curioso veio à janela ver o que era

claims.statement: Woken by the cart's loud creaking, he immediately received a tremendous slap.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang terbangun oleh deritnya itu langsung mendapat tamparan dahsyat.
claims.quote: despertado pela grande chiadeira que o carro fazia: imediatamente levou uma bofetada monumental.

claims.statement: The "Carro da Condesseira" goes about the villages and carries the witches and the devil.
claims.statement_id: "Carro da Condesseira" berkeliling desa dan membawa para penyihir serta iblis.
claims.quote: Carro da Condesseira ... anda pelas aldeias. Conduz as bruxas e o diabo.

claims.statement: The witches are inside the cart, and passing houses where people peep out at the cart, they throw their rake at them.
claims.statement_id: Para penyihir berada di dalam kereta, dan ketika melewati rumah tempat orang mengintip kereta itu, mereka melempar garu mereka ke arah orang-orang itu.
claims.quote: mesmo dentro do carro, e passando por casas, onde espreitem o carro, atiram-lhes com o restelo

claims.statement: The record cites as its source "Antígua, Tradições e Contos Populares" by Francisco Martins Sarmento, published in Guimaraes by the Sociedade Martins Sarmento in 1998.
claims.statement_id: Catatan itu menyebut sumbernya "Antígua, Tradições e Contos Populares" karya Francisco Martins Sarmento, terbitan Sociedade Martins Sarmento di Guimaraes tahun 1998.
claims.quote: SARMENTO, Francisco Martins Antígua, Tradições e Contos Populares Guimaraes, Sociedade Martins Sarmento, 1998

claims.statement: In Greek mythology Helios, son of Hyperion, was the Sun god and owned a chariot made entirely of fire drawn by four horses.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Yunani, Helios putra Hyperion adalah dewa Matahari yang memiliki kereta dari api yang ditarik empat ekor kuda.
claims.quote: Nella mitologia greca, Elio, figlio di Iperione era il dio del Sole e possedeva un carro fatto completamente di fuoco e trainato da quattro cavalli.

claims.statement: These four swift steeds of the fiery chariot, once yoked by the god, raced across the sky spreading daylight; their names were Eous (Eòo), Aethon (Etone), Phlegon (Flegone) and Pyrois (Piroide).
claims.statement_id: Keempat kuda yang sangat cepat itu, setelah dipasang oleh sang dewa, melintasi langit dan menyebarkan cahaya siang; nama mereka Eos (Eòo), Aethon (Etone), Phlegon (Flegone), dan Pyrois (Piroide).
claims.quote: Essi erano i 4 velocissimi destrieri del carro di fuoco che, aggiogati dal dio, percorrevano rapidissimi la volta celeste diffondendo la luce del giorno: Eòo Etone Flegone Piroide

claims.statement: The golden chariot of the sun was drawn across the sky by a team of four white, winged horses.
claims.statement_id: Kereta emas matahari ditarik melintasi langit oleh empat kuda putih bersayap.
claims.quote: The golden chariot of the sun was drawn across the sky drawn by a team of four white, winged horses.

claims.statement: In a translation of Ovid, the four swift horses of Sol, Aethon (Blaze), Eous (Dawn), Pyrois (Fire) and Phlegon (Flame), kick at the gates, neighing and snorting fire.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Ovid, keempat kuda cepat Sol, yaitu Aethon (Nyala), Eous (Fajar), Pyrois (Api), dan Phlegon (Lidah Api), menendang gerbang sambil meringkik dan mendengus api.
claims.quote: Meanwhile the four swift horses of Sol, Aethon (Blaze), Eous (Dawn), Pyrois (Fire) and Phlegon (Flame), kick at the gates, neighing and snorting fire

claims.statement: In the same translation the horses go forth, cleaving the clouds with beating hooves and outriding on wings the winds that blow westwards from the morning.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan yang sama kuda-kuda itu melesat keluar, membelah awan dengan derap kuku dan mendahului dengan sayap angin yang bertiup ke barat dari pagi hari.
claims.quote: Forth they go, tearing away, and cleave with beating hooves the clouds before them, and on wings outride the winds that westwards from the morning blow.

claims.statement: A Roman mythographer gives other names for the horses of Sol: Eous and Aethiops among the male trace-horses, and Bronte (thunder) and Sterope (lightning) as the female yoke-bearers.
claims.statement_id: Seorang penulis mitologi Romawi memberi nama lain bagi kuda-kuda Sol: Eous dan Aethiops di antara kuda tarik jantan, serta Bronte (guntur) dan Sterope (kilat) sebagai kuda pemikul kuk betina.
claims.quote: Names of the Horses of Sol (the Sun) [Helios]. Eous, by him the sky is turned. Aethiops, as if faming, parches the grain. These trace-horses are male. The female are yoke-bearers : Bronte, whom we call thunder (tonitrua), Sterope, whom we call lightning (fulgitrua).

claims.statement: The goddesses of the four seasons fed the solar horses ambrosia at dawn and yoked them to the heavenly chariot.
claims.statement_id: Dewi empat musim memberi kuda-kuda matahari ambrosia saat fajar dan memasangkan mereka pada kereta langit.
claims.quote: The goddesses of the four seasons fed the solar horses ambrosia at dawn and yoked them to the heavenly chariot.

claims.statement: The cavalo do pensamento ("horse of thought") is a mythical being of Portuguese legend.
claims.statement_id: Cavalo do pensamento ("kuda pikiran") adalah makhluk mitos dalam legenda Portugal.
claims.quote: O cavalo do pensamento é um ser mítico das lendas portuguesas.

claims.statement: In a tale a youth is asked to choose whether to go on the horse of the wind or the horse of thought; he chooses the horse of thought, and a horse appears that spits fire from its eyes and mouth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah kisah, seorang pemuda diminta memilih pergi dengan kuda angin atau kuda pikiran; ia memilih kuda pikiran, dan muncullah seekor kuda yang menyemburkan api dari mata dan mulutnya.
claims.quote: Bem, agora escolhe: em qual queres ir, no cavalo do vento ou no do pensamento? –O rapaz escolheu o do pensamento, e apareceu-lhe logo um cavalo que deitava fogo pelos olhos e pela boca.

claims.statement: As soon as the youth mounted the horse, it was a flight so fast that he did not know where he was going or not going.
claims.statement_id: Begitu pemuda itu menunggangi kuda itu, ia melesat sedemikian cepat sehingga ia tak tahu ke mana ia pergi dan ke mana tidak.
claims.quote: Mal o rapaz montou em cima do cavalo... aquilo era fugir que nem sabia por onde ia nem por onde não ia.

claims.statement: In the blink of an eye he found himself at his front door; when he spoke the words he had been told, the horse burst with a bang and disappeared, like an evil thing.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sekejap ia sudah berada di depan pintu rumahnya; ketika ia mengucapkan kata-kata yang dipesankan, kuda itu meledak dengan dentuman dan lenyap, seperti sesuatu yang jahat.
claims.quote: Enquanto o diabo esfrega um olho, viu-se à porta de casa. Pendurou-se como o Mouro tinha mandado, num dos ramos da figueira e disse: arre burro com todos os diabos! O cavalo deu um estoiro e desapareceu, como coisa má

claims.statement: The man of Donim was taken to the mourama and, to return to earth, had to come on the "horse of thought", which he preferred to the one "of the wind".
claims.statement_id: Lelaki dari Donim dibawa ke mourama dan, untuk kembali ke bumi, harus datang dengan "kuda pikiran", yang ia pilih daripada kuda "angin".
claims.quote: Assim, o homem de Donim foi levado para a mourama, e, para voltar à terra, teve de vir no «cavalo do pensamento», que preferiu ao «do vento».

claims.statement: Among the places listed, "cavalo do pensamento" is counted as one of 25 places in "our concelho" that are important for the mouros.
claims.statement_id: Dalam daftar tempat itu, "cavalo do pensamento" dihitung sebagai salah satu dari 25 tempat di "concelho kita" yang penting bagi para mouro.
claims.quote: Donim - pedra flutuante (23); cavalo do pensamento (24); Airão, moura em pedra flutuante (25). Aqui temos 25 lugares do nosso concelho importantes pelos mouros

claims.statement: The legend of the Cavalum concerns the Furnas do Cavalum in Machico on Madeira, large caves in basalt that popular lore says are a monster's home.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Cavalum berkisah tentang Furnas do Cavalum di Machico, pulau Madeira, gua besar di batuan basal yang menurut kepercayaan rakyat adalah tempat tinggal monster.
claims.quote: A Lenda do Cavalum é uma lenda acerca das Furnas do Cavalum, situadas na vila de Machico, na ilha da Madeira. As Furnas são umas grandes grutas escavadas em basalto que o saber popular diz que são a moradia dum monstro.

claims.statement: The Cavalum is a devil in the shape of a horse, with bat wings, that breathes fire from its nostrils.
claims.statement_id: Cavalum adalah iblis berwujud kuda, bersayap kelelawar, dan menyemburkan api dari lubang hidungnya.
claims.quote: O Cavalum é um diabo com a forma dum cavalo, com asas de morcego e que solta fogo das narinas.

claims.statement: The Cavalum told God he wanted to destroy the whole village, daring Him to thwart it.
claims.statement_id: Cavalum mengetuk pintu gereja untuk berbicara dengan Tuhan dan berkata ingin menghancurkan seluruh desa, menantang Tuhan untuk menggagalkannya.
claims.quote: foi bater à porta duma igreja para falar com Deus. No momento que Deus lhe inquiriu o porquê dele ter ido falar com ele, o Cavalum respondeu que queria destruir toda a povoação e espicaçou-O a frustá-lo.

claims.statement: The Cavalum gathered darkness against the village, causing a great storm, and neighed with glee from the clifftop at the villagers' despair.
claims.statement_id: Cavalum mengumpulkan kegelapan melawan desa hingga terjadi badai besar, dan dari puncak tebing ia meringkik gembira melihat keputusasaan warga.
claims.quote: O Cavalum reuniu então as trevas contra a povoação resultando numa grande tempestade. Do alto do penhasco, o Cavalum relinchava com regozijo defronte do desespero dos moradores.

claims.statement: So the monster would do no more harm, God imprisoned the Cavalum in the Furnas, where its angry neighing is still heard during strong storms.
claims.statement_id: Agar ia tidak lagi merusak, Tuhan memenjarakan Cavalum di Furnas, tempat ringkikan marahnya masih terdengar saat badai besar.
claims.quote: Para que o monstro não voltasse a causar estragos, Deus resolveu prender o Cavalum nas Furnas, onde ainda hoje de tempos a tempos se ouve o seu relhinchar zangado contra Deus, durante as tempestades fortes.

claims.statement: The Furnas do Cavalum caves are named after a local legend about a demon called Cavalum, who was imprisoned in the cave.
claims.statement_id: Gua Furnas do Cavalum dinamai menurut legenda setempat tentang iblis bernama Cavalum yang dipenjara di dalam gua.
claims.quote: Named after a local legend about a demon called Cavalum, who was imprisoned in the cave.

claims.statement: The Cenocroca is an imaginary animal or legendary creature often confused with the Crocotta, also called Crocuta or Crocotte.
claims.statement_id: Cenocroca adalah hewan khayalan atau makhluk legendaris yang sering tertukar dengan Crocotta, dan juga disebut Crocuta atau Crocotte.
claims.quote: La bestia Cenocroca è un animale immaginario o una creatura leggendaria. La creatura era spesso e reciprocamente confusa con la Crocotta e chiamata anche Crocuta o Crocotte.

claims.statement: It is described as having a human voice but a solid bone instead of teeth, a mouth slit to the ears, a lion's jaws and chest, an ass's body and ibex horns.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan bersuara manusia, tetapi giginya berupa satu tulang utuh, mulutnya terbelah sampai telinga, berahang dan berdada singa, bertubuh keledai, dan bertanduk ibex.
claims.quote: Viene descritta come avente la voce umana ma al posto dei denti un solido osso; un taglio della bocca che arriva fino alle orecchie, le fauci e il petto del leone, il corpo d'asino, le corna di stambecco

claims.statement: It never moved its pupils and always stared straight ahead, and with its human voice it imitated people's calls or animal cries to lure prey and devour it.
claims.statement_id: Ia tidak pernah menggerakkan pupilnya dan selalu menatap lurus ke depan, dan dengan suara manusianya ia meniru panggilan orang atau suara hewan untuk memikat mangsa lalu melahapnya.
claims.quote: Possedeva la bizzarra caratteristica di non muovere mai le pupille e di guardare sempre dinanzi a sé; con la propria voce umana imitava i richiami degli uomini o i versi degli animali per attrarre le prede e divorarle.

claims.statement: The oldest mention of a creature called Krokottas is in Strabo's Geography, describing it as a dog-wolf cross native to Ethiopia.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan tertua makhluk bernama Krokottas ada dalam Geografi karya Strabo, sebagai persilangan anjing dan serigala dari Etiopia.
claims.quote: La più antica menzione di una creatura chiamata Κροκόττας si trova all'interno della Geografia di Strabone, dove l'animale è descritto come un incrocio fra un cane e un lupo nativo dell'Etiopia.

claims.statement: The creature is also described in Umberto Eco's Il nome della rosa by the Benedictine monk Adso of Melk.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini juga digambarkan dalam Il nome della rosa karya Umberto Eco oleh biarawan Benediktin Adso dari Melk.
claims.quote: La creatura viene descritta anche all'interno de Il nome della rosa di Umberto Eco dal monaco benedettino Adso da Melk.

claims.statement: Pliny describes the crocotta as an animal that looks as though it had been produced by the union of the wolf and the dog, able to break anything with its teeth and digest it at once on swallowing.
claims.statement_id: Pliny melukiskan crocotta sebagai hewan yang tampak seolah lahir dari perkawinan serigala dan anjing, mampu mematahkan apa pun dengan giginya dan langsung mencernanya setelah menelan.
claims.quote: the crocotta, an animal which looks as though it had been produced by the union of the wolf and the dog ... for it can break any thing with its teeth, and instantly on swallowing it digest it with the stomach

claims.statement: Pliny describes the leucrocotta as a wild beast of extraordinary swiftness, the size of the wild ass, with a mouth slit up as far as the ears and one continuous bone instead of teeth, and says it is said to imitate the human voice.
claims.statement_id: Pliny melukiskan leucrocotta sebagai binatang buas yang luar biasa cepat, sebesar keledai liar, bermulut terbelah sampai ke telinga dan bergigi satu tulang menerus, dan menyebut makhluk itu konon dapat menirukan suara manusia.
claims.quote: the leucrocotta, a wild beast of extraordinary swiftness, the size of the wild ass, with the legs of a stag, the neck, tail, and breast of a lion, the head of a badger, a cloven hoof, the mouth slit up as far as the ears, and one continuous bone instead of teeth ... it is said, too, that this animal can imitate the human voice.

claims.statement: The Chipique or Chipekwe is a legendary half-snake, half-crocodile water monster living in the Zambezi river.
claims.statement_id: Chipique atau Chipekwe adalah monster air legendaris setengah ular setengah buaya yang hidup di sungai Zambezi.
claims.quote: La Chipique ou Chipekwe est un monstre aquatique légendaire, vivant dans le fleuve Zambèze, mi-serpent, mi-crocodile.

claims.statement: Its habit of overturning canoes and dragging their occupants to the bottom makes it feared by locals.
claims.statement_id: Kebiasaannya membalikkan perahu dan menyeret penumpangnya ke dasar membuatnya ditakuti penduduk setempat.
claims.quote: Son habitude de retourner les pirogues et d'entraîner leurs occupants par le fond fait qu'il est redouté des habitants locaux.

claims.statement: Despite the locals' accounts, 19th-century explorers remained sceptical of its existence.
claims.statement_id: Meski penduduk bercerita demikian, para penjelajah abad ke-19 tetap ragu akan keberadaannya.
claims.quote: Malgré leurs dires, les explorateurs du XIXe siècle sont restés sceptiques quant à son existence.

claims.statement: In European literature the animal was first mentioned by Carl Hagenbeck in 1909.
claims.statement_id: Dalam literatur Eropa, hewan ini pertama kali disebut oleh Carl Hagenbeck pada 1909.
claims.quote: Dans la littérature européenne, l'animal est cité pour la première fois par Carl Hagenbeck en 1909.

claims.statement: A serpent is said to live at the foot of Victoria Falls, as Dr. Livingstone presumed; Barotse folklore holds that this monster, the Chipique, came from the ocean, traveling over a thousand miles to rest at the falls.
claims.statement_id: Seekor ular dikatakan hidup di kaki Air Terjun Victoria, seperti dugaan Dr. Livingstone; folklor Barotse menyatakan monster ini, Chipique, datang dari samudra, menempuh lebih dari seribu mil untuk beristirahat di air terjun.
claims.quote: A serpent lives at the foot of Victoria Falls – at least, that’s what Dr. Livingstone presumed. Barotse folklore holds that this monster, the Chipique, came from the ocean, traveling over a thousand miles to rest at the falls.

claims.statement: The chipique rules the river by night and it is unsafe to approach Victoria Falls then; thirty feet long, it can easily grab a canoe and immobilize it.
claims.statement_id: Chipique menguasai sungai pada malam hari dan tidak aman mendekati Air Terjun Victoria saat itu; panjangnya tiga puluh kaki, dan ia dapat dengan mudah mencengkeram sampan dan melumpuhkannya.
claims.quote: The chipique rules the river by night, and it is unsafe to approach Victoria Falls during that time. Thirty feet in length, the chipique can easily grab a canoe and immobilize it.

claims.statement: Its head is small and slate-grey, while its serpentine, heavy body winds in black coils.
claims.statement_id: Kepalanya kecil dan berwarna abu-abu batu tulis, sedangkan tubuhnya yang seperti ular dan berat melingkar dalam gulungan hitam.
claims.quote: Its head is small and slate-grey, while its serpentine, heavy body winds in black coils.

claims.statement: Eyewitnesses include Mr. V. Pare, who saw the chipique in 1925; it reared and disappeared into a cave.
claims.statement_id: Saksi mata termasuk Mr. V. Pare, yang melihat chipique pada 1925; ia menegakkan tubuh lalu menghilang ke dalam gua.
claims.quote: Eyewitnesses include Mr. V. Pare, who saw the chipique in 1925. It reared and disappeared into a cave.

claims.statement: In the popular beliefs of central-southern Sardinia, the Coga or Bruxa (plural is Cogas) was a witch or vampire woman.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Sardinia tengah dan selatan, Coga atau Bruxa (jamak: is Cogas) adalah penyihir atau perempuan vampir.
claims.quote: Nelle credenze popolari della Sardegna centro-meridionale, la Coga o Bruxa [‘bru:ʒa] (al plurale is Cogas o is Bruxas) era la cosiddetta strega, o una donna vampiro .

claims.statement: At night they crept in groups into houses with newborns, mainly boys, to kill them.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam hari mereka berkelompok menyelinap ke rumah yang ada bayi, terutama bayi lelaki, untuk membunuhnya.
claims.quote: Durante la notte, in gruppo, si intrufolavano nelle case dove c'erano dei neonati (di sesso maschile principalmente) per ucciderli.

claims.statement: Parents laid a cane and a blessed rosary on the cradle; the Coga would start counting the rosary beads but never finish before dawn.
claims.statement_id: Orang tua menaruh tongkat buluh dan rosario yang diberkati di buaian; Coga yang datang mulai menghitung butir rosario tetapi tak pernah selesai sebelum fajar.
claims.quote: Queste creature tenebrose quando giungevano accanto alla culla iniziavano a contare i grani del rosario, senza però mai riuscire a contarli tutti prima dell'alba

claims.statement: A coga is said to be the seventh daughter of a family of only girls.
claims.statement_id: Konon coga adalah anak perempuan ketujuh dalam keluarga yang hanya punya anak perempuan.
claims.quote: Si narra che una coga sia la settima figlia di una famiglia nella quale sono nate solo femmine.

claims.statement: The Cogas looked like old hags but were recognised mainly by a little tail they had from birth, and could take any form.
claims.statement_id: Cogas tampak seperti nenek sihir tua, tetapi dikenali dari ekor kecil sejak lahir, dan dapat berubah menjadi wujud apa pun.
claims.quote: Le Cogas avevano l'aspetto di vecchie megere ma si riconoscevano soprattutto perché avevano un piccolo pezzo di coda da quando erano nate e avevano la capacità di assumere qualsiasi forma.

claims.statement: Villacidro, capital of the Province of Medio Campidano, is famed for its nickname Sa bidda de is cogas, "the village of the cogas".
claims.statement_id: Villacidro, ibu kota Provinsi Medio Campidano, terkenal dengan julukan Sa bidda de is cogas, "desa para coga".
claims.quote: Villacidro, capoluogo della Provincia del Medio Campidano, è rinomato per il suo appellativo: Sa bidda de is cogas.

claims.statement: According to Marcialis, they anointed their joints with melted lard to turn into animals, cats or flies.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Marcialis, mereka mengolesi sendi tubuhnya dengan lemak babi yang dilelehkan untuk berubah menjadi hewan, kucing, atau lalat.
claims.quote: si ungevano le giunture del corpo per trasformarsi in animali, gatti o mosche.

claims.statement: Objects placed upside down in the house, such as a broom or trivet, drove off the coga, which disliked disorder and might even die at the sight.
claims.statement_id: Benda yang diletakkan terbalik di rumah, seperti sapu atau tungku berkaki tiga, mengusir coga karena ia tidak suka kekacauan dan bisa mati melihatnya.
claims.quote: Si diceva che la coga, non essendo amante del disordine, alla vista di questi oggetti si sarebbe allontanata o addirittura sarebbe morta.

claims.statement: The Cogas can be linked with Lilith, an ancient Sumerian deity who in Jewish culture is a female demon.
claims.statement_id: Sosok Cogas dapat dikaitkan dengan Lilith, dewi Sumeria kuno yang dalam budaya Yahudi adalah iblis perempuan.
claims.quote: La figura delle Cogas può essere associata a quella di Lilith antica divinità sumera, che per la cultura ebraica è un demone femminile

claims.statement: In ancient times there existed is cogas, the coghe (witches): women who lived normal lives but on particular occasions could transform into animals, especially flies and cats, by anointing their bodies with certain unguents.
claims.statement_id: Pada zaman dahulu ada is cogas, para coghe (penyihir): perempuan yang hidup biasa tetapi pada kesempatan tertentu dapat berubah menjadi hewan, terutama lalat dan kucing, dengan mengolesi tubuh mereka dengan salep tertentu.
claims.quote: In ancient times, there existed is cogas, the coghe (witches). They were women who lived normal lives but who, on particular occasions, could transform into animals, especially flies and cats, by anointing their bodies with certain unguents.

claims.statement: Once transformed, they would enter the rooms where infants slept, sucking their blood and leaving them exhausted and sometimes dead.
claims.statement_id: Setelah berubah, mereka masuk ke kamar tempat bayi tidur, menghisap darahnya dan membuat mereka kelelahan dan kadang mati.
claims.quote: Once transformed, they would enter the rooms where infants slept, sucking their blood, leaving them exhausted and sometimes dead.

claims.statement: The most common remedies included placing an inverted tripod in front of the door, leaning an upside-down broom against it, or leaving an old, toothless sickle so that the coga would stop to count the teeth; since she could only count to seven, she always had to start over until the night passed.
claims.statement_id: Penangkal yang paling umum antara lain meletakkan tripod terbalik di depan pintu, menyandarkan sapu terbalik padanya, atau meninggalkan sabit tua tak bergigi agar coga berhenti menghitung giginya; karena ia hanya bisa menghitung sampai tujuh, ia selalu harus mengulang sampai malam berlalu.
claims.quote: The most common remedies included placing an inverted tripod in front of the door, leaning an upside-down broom against it, or leaving an old, toothless sickle so that the coga would stop to count the teeth. However, since she could only count to seven, she always had to start over until the night passed

claims.statement: The most powerful defense was the invocation to San Sisinnio.
claims.statement_id: Perlindungan yang paling ampuh adalah doa kepada San Sisinnio.
claims.quote: But the most powerful defense was the invocation to San Sisinnio.

claims.statement: The confinati or anime confinate ("confined souls") are mythical figures of the folk traditions of north-eastern Lombardy, especially the Bergamo valleys, Val Camonica and Valtellina.
claims.statement_id: Confinati atau anime confinate ("jiwa terbuang") adalah tokoh mitos dalam tradisi rakyat Lombardia timur laut, terutama di lembah Bergamo, Val Camonica, dan Valtellina.
claims.quote: Confinati oppure le anime confinate sono delle figure mitiche diffuse nelle tradizioni popolari della Lombardia nord-orientale, soprattutto nelle Valli Bergamasche, Val Camonica e Valtellina.

claims.statement: They were the souls of dissatisfied dead, banished by exorcism to remote, inhospitable side valleys so they could not harm the living.
claims.statement_id: Mereka arwah orang mati yang tidak tenang, yang diusir lewat eksorsisme ke lembah samping yang tak ramah agar tidak mengganggu orang hidup.
claims.quote: Essi erano delle anime di persone morte insoddisfatte, che erano state mandate al confino tramite un esorcismo in vallate laterali ed inospitali, in modo tale da non poter nuocere ai vivi.

claims.statement: In Lombard they are called cunfinàcc (eastern) or cunfinàa (western).
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Lombard mereka disebut cunfinàcc (timur) atau cunfinàa (barat).
claims.quote: In lombardo sono chiamati cunfinàcc (orientale) cunfinàa (occidentale).

claims.statement: In Valtellina there is a belief in the "confined" souls, relegated to anything but welcoming places to serve there the eternal penalty they deserve.
claims.statement_id: Di Valtellina ada kepercayaan pada jiwa-jiwa "terkurung", yang dibuang ke tempat yang sama sekali tidak ramah untuk menjalani hukuman abadi yang pantas mereka terima.
claims.quote: interessante di tale elaborazione ... in Valtellina, la credenza nei ... nelle anima “confinate”, relegate in luoghi tutt’altro che accoglienti, per scontare ... l’eterna pena meritata.

claims.statement: In one variant the spirit, often a "colony" of spirits, is nailed to a wearying and desperate penalty: often digging gold or metals, splitting stones, striking boulders with mallets, or carrying enormous rocks on their shoulders.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu varian roh itu, sering berupa "koloni" roh, terpaku pada hukuman yang melelahkan dan putus asa: sering menggali emas atau logam, memecah batu, memukul bongkahan dengan palu besar, atau memikul batu raksasa di bahu.
claims.quote: lo presenta (o li presenta, ... spesso si tratta di una “colonia” di spiriti) inchiodato ad una pena faticosa e disperata (spesso cavare oro o metalli, spaccare pietre, battere con mazze contro macigni, portare enormi massi sulle spalle

claims.statement: According to other variants these spirits go on acting to the harm of people, frightening them with noises or screams, turning huts upside down ("a soqquadro le baite") and hindering their passage in certain places, generally by hurling rocks on them.
claims.statement_id: Menurut varian lain, roh-roh ini terus bertindak merugikan manusia, menakut-nakuti mereka dengan bunyi atau jeritan, mengobrak-abrik pondok ("a soqquadro le baite"), dan menghalangi jalan mereka di tempat tertentu, umumnya dengan menjatuhkan batu ke atas mereka.
claims.quote: Secondo altre ancora, infine, questi spiriti conservano una certa ... e continuano a manifestare la loro ... a danno degli uomini, spaventandoli con rumori od urla, mettendo a soqquadro le baite, ostacolando in vario modo il loro transito in certi luoghi o le loro ... (in genere, rovesciando loro addosso massi).

claims.statement: The only but sure way to defend oneself is prayer, even in the extremely concise form of the sign of the cross.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya cara yang pasti untuk membela diri adalah doa, bahkan dalam bentuk paling ringkas berupa tanda salib.
claims.quote: Unico, ma sicuro modo per difendersi, ... la preghiera, anche nella forma estremamente sintetica del segno di croce.

claims.statement: A hidden plateau called Piana dei Dannati or Piana di Zana hosts the cunfinàa of the Corni Rossi; anyone passing there at night might hear them beating their mallets endlessly on the countless stones.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah dataran tersembunyi bernama Piana dei Dannati atau Piana di Zana menampung para cunfinàa dari Corni Rossi; siapa pun yang lewat di sana pada malam hari mungkin mendengar mereka memukulkan palu tanpa henti pada batu yang tak terhitung.
claims.quote: si trova un pianoro nascosto, detto Piana dei Dannati o Piana di Zana, che ospita i ... dei Corni Rossi. Chi passasse di qui nottetempo potrebbe udirli battere senza sosta le loro mazze sulle innumerevoli pietre

claims.statement: In Ibizan folk mythology a crespell is a monstrous being living in groups in caves; crespells have warty bodies, grunt and shoot fire from their eyes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi rakyat Ibiza, crespell adalah makhluk mengerikan yang hidup berkelompok di gua; tubuhnya penuh kutil, mereka menggeram, dan menyemburkan api dari mata.
claims.quote: A la mitologia popular eivissenca, un crespell és un ésser monstruós que viu en grup a les coves. Els crespells tenen el cos ple de berrugues, grunyen i treuen foc pels ulls.

claims.statement: These little monsters live in the Cova des Crespells at Buscastell.
claims.statement_id: Monster-monster kecil ini tinggal di Cova des Crespells di Buscastell.
claims.quote: Aquests petits monstres viuen dins la Cova des Crespells, situada a Buscastell.

claims.statement: Mothers threatened naughty children with these creatures, which supposedly come out at night and eat small children.
claims.statement_id: Para ibu menakuti anak nakal dengan makhluk ini, yang konon muncul pada malam hari dan memakan anak kecil.
claims.quote: Les mares "amenaçaven" els nens que es portaven malament amb aquestes criatures, que suposadament apareixen durant la nit i es mengen els nens petits.

issues.message: Di bawah target core: 1 sumber (target 2). gaps sudah diisi; nilai apakah pencariannya memadai.

claims.statement: The crieurs or appeleurs are a group of nocturnal creatures of myth and folklore whose shared trait is shouting or calling to travellers, either to lure them into traps or to warn them of danger.
claims.statement_id: Crieur atau appeleur adalah sekelompok makhluk malam dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat yang sama-sama berteriak atau memanggil pejalan, entah untuk menjebak atau memperingatkan bahaya.
claims.quote: Les crieurs, ou appeleurs, forment un ensemble de créatures nocturnes issues de la mythologie et du folklore populaire, dont la caractéristique commune est de crier ou d'apostropher les voyageurs, soit pour les attirer dans des pièges, soit pour les avertir d'un danger.

claims.statement: Pierre Dubois offers a storyteller's explanation: the appeleurs are heralds of fairyland whose mission was to warn humans of their murderous folly.
claims.statement_id: Pierre Dubois memberi penjelasan ala pendongeng: para appeleur adalah bentara dunia peri yang bertugas memperingatkan manusia akan kegilaan mereka yang mematikan.
claims.quote: Pierre Dubois pense qu'il n'en est rien, et donne une explication de conteur : les appeleurs seraient les hérauts du monde de féerie, leur mission consistant à prévenir les hommes de leur folie meurtrière.

claims.statement: Usually described as lutins or revenants, they can take many human or animal forms.
claims.statement_id: Mereka umumnya digambarkan sebagai lutin atau arwah, dan dapat mengambil banyak wujud manusia atau hewan.
claims.quote: Généralement décrits comme des lutins ou des revenants, ils peuvent revêtir de très nombreuses formes humanoïdes ou animales.

claims.statement: They are called hupeu or lupeux in Berry, houppeux in Picardy, houpou in Haute-Bretagne, crieux in Maine and Anjou, and hueur in the Limousin.
claims.statement_id: Namanya hupeu atau lupeux di Berry, houppeux di Picardie, houpou di Haute-Bretagne, crieux di Maine dan Anjou, dan hueur di Limousin.
claims.quote: Le nom employé est hupeu ou lupeux dans le Berry, houppeux en Picardie, houpou en Haute-Bretagne, crieux dans le Maine et l'Anjou, hueur dans le Limousin

claims.statement: The hupeur or hueur is a fabulous night bird of French folklore that nests near ponds and marshes; at nightfall it cries with a human voice to lure lost walkers.
claims.statement_id: Hupeur atau hueur adalah burung malam khayalan dalam cerita rakyat Prancis yang bersarang dekat kolam dan rawa; saat malam tiba ia berteriak dengan suara manusia untuk memikat pejalan yang tersesat.
claims.quote: Le hupeur, ou hueur, est un oiseau nocturne fabuleux du folklore français, qui niche près des étangs et des marais. Lorsque la nuit tombe, il se met à crier d'une voix humaine pour attirer les promeneurs égarés.

claims.statement: It then changes shape to push and drown the careless victim, before returning to its first form to find another.
claims.statement_id: Ia lalu berubah wujud untuk mendorong dan menenggelamkan orang yang lengah, kemudian kembali ke wujud semula untuk mencari korban lain.
claims.quote: Il se transforme alors pour pousser et noyer l'imprudent, puis reprend son apparence première afin de trouver une autre victime.

claims.statement: George Sand mentions the creature in her rustic legends: in Berry the lupeux repeats "Ah! Ah!" until someone answers.
claims.statement_id: George Sand menyebut makhluk ini dalam legenda pedesaannya: di Berry, lupeux terus berseru "Ah! Ah!" sampai ada yang menjawab.
claims.quote: George Sand évoque cette créature dans ses légendes rustiques : dans le Berry, le lupeux répète Ah ! Ah ! jusqu'à ce qu'on lui réponde.

claims.statement: The moine de Saire looks like a little man in a white tailcoat; sometimes he appears in the Cherbourg roadstead as if drowning, begging sailors for help.
claims.statement_id: Moine de Saire tampak seperti lelaki kecil berjas putih; kadang ia muncul di teluk Cherbourg seolah tenggelam dan memohon pertolongan para pelaut.
claims.quote: Le moine de Saire a l'apparence d'un petit homme en frac blanc. Tantôt, il apparaît dans la rade de Cherbourg où il semble se noyer, suppliant les matelots et les marins de l'aider.

claims.statement: The legend is found everywhere in many variants sharing the theme of night and its dangers.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini ada di mana-mana dalam berbagai versi yang sama-sama berkisar pada malam dan bahayanya.
claims.quote: Cette légende est universellement présente sous diverses variantes qui ont pour point commun la nuit et ses dangers.
